builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Replica-Aware Split Inference for Edge IoT Systems
summary: The method replaces ad hoc or greedy replica re-hosting of TinyML model segments after an IoT device failure with a MILP formulation that jointly selects replica hosts and communication protocols to minimize post-reconfiguration latency under memory constraints. The cost is solving a mixed-integer linear program at recovery time, which requires centralized knowledge of the network state and adds solver latency and orchestration complexity to the failure-recovery path. It can fail if link rates or device capabilities drift from the modeled values used by the optimizer, if solver time exceeds the tolerable recovery window, or if flash and runtime memory on surviving devices is insufficient for the chosen replicas.
rationale: The technique targets fault-tolerant distributed inference across heterogeneous IoT microcontrollers, which is outside the reader's production scope of GPU- or API-hosted model serving.
technique: Replica-aware fault recovery for split TinyML inference

claims.statement: The method replaces ad hoc or greedy replica re-hosting of TinyML model segments after an IoT device failure with a MILP formulation that jointly selects replica hosts and communication protocols to minimize post-reconfiguration latency under memory constraints. The cost is solving a mixed-integer linear program at recovery time, which requires centralized knowledge of the network state and adds solver latency and orchestration complexity to the failure-recovery path. It can fail if link rates or device capabilities drift from the modeled values used by the optimizer, if solver time exceeds the tolerable recovery window, or if flash and runtime memory on surviving devices is insufficient for the chosen replicas.

MILP-based replica placement achieves average modeled end-to-end inference latency 6.8% lower than a Computation Greedy baseline and 18.3% lower than Random placement after device failure, in simulations with MobileNetV2 on 15 IoT devices.
